solutions.check: 32 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: He had a member removed from the UN (Uche)

indicators.note: taking something from a phrase means lifting a run of its letters straight out of it

parts.note: the last letter of 'the', then 'UN', then the start of the name in brackets

explanation.surface: A UN delegate called Uche has had a member of his team expelled from the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is thE UN UCHe; 'member' looks like a delegate, but the definition means a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated man has literally lost a part of his body, which the setter calls a member.

clue.text: Old lover? Well, don't hold your breath

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
hale means healthy, in good shape

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to wait eagerly for a former lover's return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a throat-clearing interjection, but it is an adjective meaning healthy. 'Don't hold your breath' is usually an idiom for 'don't expect it'; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing air from the lungs is the opposite of keeping it in, so the instruction literally describes breathing out.

clue.text: (11ac./27ac.) Pence, able to shake booty, accepts ring as prestigious award

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other
to shake something is to jumble it up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
something captured, such as a ship taken in war

explanation.surface: US Vice-President Mike Pence, able to wiggle his backside, wins a famous award.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring goes in among the letters of 'Pence, able', and all ten are mixed to make NOBEL PEACE; booty adds PRIZE. 'Booty' looks like slang for a backside, which is what 'shake' wants.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel Peace Prize is among the most famous international honours, given annually in Oslo for work towards ending conflict.

clue.text: Stupid person nursing awful dose — result of coronavirus?

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, cradled in the arms, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a clown is a fool

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so these letters are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot is looking after someone suffering a nasty dose of illness during the pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' and 'dose' suit the medical surface, which makes the dose easy to miss as material to be rearranged and tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: During the 2020 pandemic businesses shut their doors, so a shutdown of operations was an outcome of the virus; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Cost of getting Katie and Mark together?

indicators.note: putting two things together joins them side by side, one after the other

parts.note: Katie Price is a British glamour model and reality TV personality
a tag is a label or mark

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how expensive it would be to set Katie up with a man called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Katie Price, a much-married British celebrity, makes 'getting together' sound like a romance; 'Mark' is a common noun, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A price tag is the label stating what something is sold for, and by extension the expense of anything.

clue.text: It's hairy, Buzz mounting Grant

indicators.note: in a down entry, to mount is to sit on top, so the first piece goes above the second

parts.note: to buzz someone is to give them a ring on the phone
to grant permission is to let

explanation.surface: Buzz, a hairy creature, is mounting another called Grant, as if an astronaut and a man were coupling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' and 'Grant' look like names, as in Buzz Aldrin and Hugh Grant, but both are ordinary verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral curl of hair, so it is literally a thing made of hair.

clue.text: A tit's place: by the old man's drink?

parts.note: a breast sits in the cup of a bra
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Where does a small bird belong? Perched beside Dad's glass, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tit' suggests the bird, but it is slang for a breast. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is an informal British name for a cup of tea, the everyday hot beverage.

clue.text: Loathsome person's penis — don't eat it!

parts.note: a toad is a contemptible person; the 's is kept
tool is vulgar slang for the penis

explanation.surface: A warning not to eat the private parts of some repulsive individual.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a warning rather than a synonym: it describes the thing by what you should not do with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Many wild fungi of this kind are poisonous, so the warning against consuming one describes it fairly.

clue.text: Drunk eyed girl in a piggish way

indicators.note: someone drunk is unsteady and muddled, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy man ogled a young woman in a boorish, swinish manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piggish' fits the leering surface as rude, but here it means like a pig at a trough.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs are proverbially gluttonous, so eating or wanting things like a pig means doing it with excessive appetite.

clue.text: Whack Rex's kitchen aid

parts.note: a whack is a share or portion, as is a slice
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone tells us to hit a gadget belonging to a man named Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whack' looks like a verb meaning hit, but it is the noun meaning a portion, as in 'a fair whack'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slicer is a utensil for cutting bread, meat or vegetables, the sort of gadget used when cooking.

clue.text: Hotplate exploded — bingo! — over head of Lord Gnome

indicators.note: in an across entry, being over something means coming before it in reading order here

parts.note: a hob is the cooking surface on top of a stove

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these letters are blown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Lord

explanation.surface: A cooker blows up – there you go! – and the blast flies over the proprietor's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is the fictional proprietor of Private Eye, where this puzzle appears; only 'Gnome' is the definition. The jumbled letters of BINGO plus L make GOBLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a mischievous little sprite of folklore, the same family of small mythical creatures as a garden dwarf.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Large, seedy, eastern European city

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
seedy can mean unwell
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A description of a big, rundown city somewhere in Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern European' reads as one phrase, but the comma before it is a clue: 'eastern' gives E and the city is in France, not the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France near the Belgian border, so it is a place on the continent.

clue.text: US state briefly declined morally and gave way

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the end of the word is dropped

parts.note: Colo. is the old abbreviation for Colorado
to lapse is to fall from a moral standard

explanation.surface: An American state slid into moral decline and gave in.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened state name loses its last letter to leave COL.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure that falls down has given way under its load, so the two phrases describe the same failure.

clue.text: see 21dn.
Fanciful, getting fresh just before end of day

indicators.note: one thing placed before another sits ahead of it in the reading order

parts.note: a fresh room is airy
just means fair, as a judgement

indicators.note: the end of something is its final part, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Someone grows cheeky or flirtatious right before the day draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just before' reads as one phrase meaning shortly before; here 'just' is FAIR and 'before' only places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy describes ideas that are vague, impractical and unrealistic, the same sense as imaginative and unrealistic.

clue.text: Dope going round block for wrapping material

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: a nit, or nitwit, is a fool
to foil a plan is to block it

explanation.surface: Drugs are passed around the housing block in their wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs and 'block' a building, but they are a fool and a verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil, now usually aluminium, is the thin metal sheet used for covering food in the kitchen.

clue.text: Go off with a Stalin white-washed version of the past?

indicators.note: food gone off has spoilt, so these letters turn into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stalin rewrote history and airbrushed enemies out of photos; someone storms off at such a whitewash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Go' is fodder and 'off' the signal. Stalin's doctored history makes the definition doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for former times that tends to forget their bad side, an idealised memory.

clue.text: Dick makes an appearance at the end of his act?

definitions.text: Dick makes an appearance at the end of his act?

parts.words: Dick makes an appearance at the end of his act?
parts.note: surface reading: a man named Dick comes on stage for a curtain call
setter's reading: dick is slang for the penis, which a male performer who undresses finally reveals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' looks like a man's name; the question mark warns of the vulgar second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A male performer who removes clothes on stage ends his routine fully naked, exposing his genitals.

clue.text: City contributes to senator on tour

indicators.note: what contributes to something forms part of it, so the word is a stretch inside the phrase

parts.note: the run spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A city makes a donation to a politician who is travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is senaTOR ON TOur.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada, capital of the province of Ontario.

clue.text: One appears in New Moon and Love the Land of Trump — sinister

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be seen within it, so one piece sits inside another
something new is made afresh, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
Donald Trump was president of the United States

explanation.surface: A fan who loves Trump's America turns up in a film or poem about a new moon, which is sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' would normally give O, but every letter is already accounted for, so here it is surface padding between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous describes something threatening, foreboding harm, which is close to sinister in its sense of menace.

clue.text: Clue: S&M involved power

indicators.note: involved can mean complicated and tangled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, the ampersand ignored

explanation.surface: A hint that sadomasochism was part of the power games in a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: The ampersand contributes no letters; only the S and M count.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means strength or influence, as in political muscle, so it stands in for force or might.

clue.text: (& 14ac.) Hard work, getting party to follow instructions

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: a book of instructions
the party is one of the UK's two main political parties, the one founded to represent working people

explanation.surface: Getting a political party to obey orders is a heavy task.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'follow' as 'obey'; it only means the party comes after the instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual labour is physical toil done by hand, the strenuous kind of job that tires the body.

clue.text: A party offence to back lordly politician

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: to go back is to go the other way, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or transgression

explanation.surface: A party wrongdoing is used to support a politician from the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To back' looks like 'to support', but it turns the offence round. Andrew Adonis is a Labour member of the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Adonis is a British Labour peer and former minister, so he is a member of the upper house active in politics.

clue.text: Little data on aroused state — about to go for coronavirus?

indicators.note: little means short, so the word is cut off before its last letter
something told to go must leave, so those letters are removed

parts.note: info is short for information, or data
a sexual response in a man
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Scant information about a state of excitement, and whether the virus is set to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' trims a word by its last letter, and RE is the usual crossword word for 'about'. 'Aroused state' sounds innocent but is a sexual response.
explanation.definitionFit: Covid-19 is caught by catching a virus, so it is one example of a disease passed between people; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Conservative with wind — fishy thing

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to reel in a line is to wind it

explanation.surface: A flatulent Tory is something suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests flatulence and 'fishy' suspicion; both are angling terms here.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket an angler carries the catch in, so it is an object closely tied to fish.

clue.text: Maybe Tony's one to pull back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to draw a cart is to pull it
a means one

explanation.surface: Perhaps Tony Blair is the person to retreat, or to win back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tony is the American theatre prize, not a man; 'Maybe' says it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is the annual honour for Broadway theatre, so it is one instance of a prize.

clue.text: Having certain members injured (hospital avoided)

indicators.note: what is avoided is kept away from, so that letter is left out

parts.note: harmed means hurt
H is the map sign for hospital

explanation.surface: Some limbs were hurt, but the casualties stayed away from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' are limbs, so having arms is one way of having some.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed literally means possessing arms, the upper limbs, which are particular members of the body.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Ring kitchen equipment bloke who's a staunch Protestant

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
a range is a large cooking stove
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: Phone the man who sells kitchen appliances, a devout churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like an instruction to phone, but it is the letter O. An Orangeman belongs to the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity strong in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order are committed unionist Protestants, so the name stands for a hard-line one.

clue.text: 'Hattersley with an agenda'? Not how you'd describe Corbyn

parts.note: Roy Hattersley is a former deputy leader of the Labour Party
an and a are the same article
an agenda is a list of items

explanation.surface: A Labour grandee with a hidden plan is unlike Jeremy Corbyn, the left-wing former Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is negative: Corbyn is a known republican, so a supporter of the monarchy is what he is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist supports the monarchy, whereas Corbyn has long favoured abolishing it, so the label does not fit him.

clue.text: Drat! I maligned penis — ultimately, it's much bigger than you might think

definitions.text: it's much bigger than you might think

indicators.note: to malign is to twist something's reputation, so these letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of penis

explanation.surface: A man cursing that his penis was insulted insists it is larger than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the Doctor's time machine in the BBC series Doctor Who, a police box far larger inside than out.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who's police-box time machine famously holds a vast interior within a small exterior, so it is bigger than it seems.
